study type: Clinical Practice Guideline based on a systematic review
exposure: Nonpharmacological methods for pain management during labour and delivery (e.g., ambulation, massage, stroking, water, vibrations, acupressure, sterile water injections, deep massage, labour support, yoga, relaxation, visualization, breathing, auto-hypnosis, cognitive restructuring, music, odors, biofeedback, Lamaze, Bonapace, prenatal training, gymnastic, chanting, haptonomy, supportive environment, TENS, antenatal education)
cohort: This is a review/guideline; the evidence reviewed pertains to women experiencing pain during labour and delivery.
finding: Nonpharmacological approaches are recommended as safe and effective first-line methods for pain management during childbirth, contributing to reduced interventions, improved coping mechanisms, and enhanced maternal and newborn well-being by activating neurophysiologic and endocrine resources.
mod_finding: Nonpharmacological pain management during childbirth can lead to a reduction in the need for obstetrical interventions, labour augmentation, or Caesarean section.
